correctness.rationale: Both the witness and the all-forms lower bound check out. Over the algebraic closure, X=0 and the last two partials would force Y=Z=0. Otherwise the first two partials force Y=Z=2X and the last is X³≠0. This proves geometric smoothness; plane components would intersect by Bézout and create a singularity, so the quartic is geometrically irreducible, with genus three. The projective point list is complete by normalizing the last nonzero coordinate. For each form there is exactly one first-nonzero-coefficient normalization; the finite census tests each rational zero and includes only nonzero gradients, whose lines are the tangents by the hypersurface formula. A separately written exact modular computation exhausted 31, 3906 and 2441406 forms and found zero filling cases, with maximum coverages 6, 21 and 29. It independently found 11 quartic points, 11 distinct tangent lines and union size 31. In particular, six of those lines already comprise a complete pencil, consistent with the assertion concerning the union of all eleven.
residual_risks: The finite census certifies only the specified field and degrees; geometric smoothness is established separately, not inferred from the finite points.

Even the independently obtained sharp cubic coverage count is covered by the matching records. No genuine valuable remainder survives as a repair of the submitted claim.
residual_risks: This failure concerns incremental scientific value as submitted, not the usefulness of the underlying extremal question or the validity of the corroborating computation.
